rules.title: Annotation argument literal kinds
rules.statement: An annotation argument literal is one of: integer literal, float literal, bool literal, string literal, an enum literal `Name::Variant`, or an array literal `[lit, ...]` of nested literals. Array elements are parsed recursively.

rules.title: Float annotation literal suffix and underscores
rules.statement: A float annotation literal has its digit-group `_` separators removed and an optional trailing `f32`/`f64` suffix stripped before being parsed as a double.

rules.title: String annotation literal escapes
rules.statement: A quoted string annotation literal has its surrounding `"` removed and the escapes `\n \t \r \\ \" \0` decoded; any other `\X` sequence is preserved verbatim as `\X`. A raw string `r"..."` strips the `r"` prefix and trailing `"` with no escape processing.

rules.title: Bare annotation has no arguments
rules.statement: `#[A]` with neither an args list nor a `= value` produces an annotation instance with no field bindings.

rules.title: Equals-value annotation binds first field
rules.statement: `#[A = lit]` binds `lit` to the annotation datatype's first declared field. If the datatype has no fields it is an error (`annotation '{A}' takes no arguments`).

rules.title: Positional annotation args match fields in declaration order
rules.statement: In `#[A(args...)]`, positional arguments bind to the annotation datatype's fields in declaration order. Supplying more positional args than fields is an error (`takes at most {n} positional args`).

rules.title: Named annotation args match by field name
rules.statement: In `#[A(key = lit, ...)]`, a named argument binds `lit` to the field named `key`; an unknown field name is an error (`annotation '{A}' has no field '{key}'`) and that argument is skipped.

rules.title: User annotations resolve to #[annotation]-marked datatypes
rules.statement: An item-level annotation whose name resolves to a datatype is materialized as an annotation instance only if that datatype is itself marked `#[annotation]`; the `#[annotation]` marker sets the datatype's annotation-type flag. Names not resolving to such a datatype are silently ignored.

rules.title: Annotations attach to the next item
rules.statement: Annotations accumulate and apply to the next non-annotation, non-doc item; after that item is lowered the pending annotation buffer is cleared.

rules.title: #[type_code=N] assigns an explicit struct/datatype type code
rules.statement: `#[type_code=N]` on a struct or datatype sets its type code to N and registers it under the fully-qualified name `pkg::Name` for cross-package `type_code_of::<T>()` resolution.

rules.title: #[tag_dispatch(system)] on a trait
rules.statement: `#[tag_dispatch(system_name)]` on a trait records the named tag-dispatch system for that trait.

rules.title: #[type_code=N] on a trait makes it a genos
rules.statement: `#[type_code=N]` on a trait stores the code on the trait; the code identifies a logical datatype family that each `impl Trait for T` propagates to its target struct during lowering.

rules.title: #[type_code] forbidden on a parametric genos template
rules.statement: `#[type_code=N]` on a trait that has type parameters (a template/parametric genos) is an error; it must be attached to a concrete specialization `#[type_code=N] genos T<Args>;`.

rules.title: Structural struct attribute flags are monotone set
rules.statement: The structural attribute flags `#[zone_mut] #[zoned2] #[rel_ptr] #[self_describing] #[borrow_carrying]` may only set (never clear) the corresponding struct flag, and apply to every specialization of a struct as well as to base structs.

rules.title: #[zoned] promotes a struct to a zoned datatype
rules.statement: A `struct` carrying a `#[zoned]` attribute is lowered as a zoned datatype (IS_ZONED set) with annotation fields applied, equivalent to a `datatype`/`eidos` declaration.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: zoned/datatype types are not present in Rust.

rules.title: datatype declarations are zoned
rules.statement: A `datatype`/`eidos` declaration is always lowered with the IS_ZONED flag set.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: datatype/eidos kind has no Rust analog.

rules.title: Concrete datatype auto type code from name hash
rules.statement: A concrete (non-generic) zoned datatype/struct with no explicit type code is auto-assigned a 56-bit code derived from the hash of its canonical name `pkg::Name`; codes below 128 are shifted into the >=128 range to avoid the reserved inline-AnyVal range 1..127. Generic templates receive their code at instantiation time.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: type codes have no Rust analog.

rules.title: instantiate declaration requires a generic target with concrete args
rules.statement: `instantiate T;` / `pub instantiate T;` pins a monomorphization root. The target must resolve to a struct, datatype, or enum; `instantiate T;` on a non-generic type (no type arguments) is an error. `pub` marks the pin for library re-export.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: explicit `instantiate` (C++ `template class Foo<int>;` analog).

rules.title: Bodyless struct/datatype instantiation requires concrete type arguments
rules.statement: A bodyless `struct Foo<...>;` / `datatype Foo<...>;` (no NAME, only a generic-inst type) is an explicit instantiation: every type argument must be concrete. A `Foo<T>` with an unbound type variable is an error directing the user to write a generic definition with a body. A bare `struct Foo;` referring to an undefined name is an error.

rules.title: Bodyless genos specialization declaration
rules.statement: A bodyless trait-position decl `#[type_code=N] genos T<Args>;` (no NAME, TYPE is a generic-inst over a trait name) declares a genos specialization: it must carry type arguments, all of which must resolve, and the type_code is registered against the like-named eidos/struct's mangled and canonical names (including under the template's home package when it differs).
rules.divergence: Logos addition: genos/eidos has no Rust analog.

rules.title: union lowered as struct
rules.statement: A `union` definition is lowered through the same path as a struct (identical field shape); layout/unsafe-gating is deferred.
rules.uncertainty: Slice-1 behavior; union soundness gating is a noted follow-up, so semantics may change.

rules.title: extern block children flattened into the item stream
rules.statement: An `extern { ... }` block is not itself an item; its child extern-fn declarations are spliced inline, in order, into the module's item worklist for lowering.

rules.title: Outer doc comments attach to next item
rules.statement: Outer doc comments `///` (line) and `/** */` (block) accumulate, stripping the marker prefix and joining lines with `\n`, and attach to the next lowered item.

rules.title: Inner doc comments attach to the module
rules.statement: Inner doc comments `//!` (line) and `/*! */` (block) accumulate into a module-level inner-doc buffer (stripping marker and one leading space, joining with `\n`) and are committed as the module's documentation after all items.

rules.title: cfg attributes drop items
rules.statement: An item whose `#[cfg(...)]` predicate evaluates false is dropped (not lowered), discarding its pending annotations and doc; this enables same-name platform switches such as `#[cfg(unix)]`/`#[cfg(windows)]`.

rules.title: Test attributes on functions
rules.statement: `#[test]`, `#[ignore]`, and `#[should_panic]` on a function tag it accordingly; `#[should_panic(expected = "...")]` records the expected panic substring (a quoted string literal).

rules.title: static defines global storage
rules.statement: `static` defines real global storage emitted as one global symbol per item (versus `const`, which is inlined at each use). `static mut` is mutable; a `static` without an initializer value is external. The symbol is module-qualified (falling back to `pkg$name`).

rules.title: const carries an inlined value
rules.statement: `const` definitions carry a name, type, and value expression; the value is inlined at each use site.
